Right then, it’s over to the Bangladesh batters now. Their first challenge will be to negotiate the Irish quicks before the spinners come into play. It's still early in the day, and it remains to be seen how the pitch behaves as the day progresses. Ireland will be hunting for early wickets to put the hosts on the back foot, and it will be crucial for them to grab every chance that comes their way if they are to take a first-innings lead. Back in a bit for Bangladesh's reply.

If not for the lower-order resistance from Barry McCarthy and Jordan Neill after the wobble in the middle, the visiting side might well have been restricted to around 250. They could only add 16 runs to their overnight score, but will not be too unhappy with this total. The hosts were far from their best in the field early on and could have bowled Ireland out for less had they held on to their chances. All six bowling options used by Najmul Hossain Shanto picked up at least one wicket. Mehidy Hasan Miraz led the way with 3 wickets, while the left-arm spin duo of Hasan Murad and Taijul Islam chipped in with two wickets each.

Bangladesh needed just 14 legal balls, and inside 15 minutes today, Ireland have been bowled out for 286. The visitors will have mixed feelings about this total. From 222/7, they did well to reach 286, but had the batters converted their starts, they could have easily pushed past the 300 mark. The Irish innings was a story of batters getting starts but failing to convert them into the big score the tourists needed. Paul Stirling and debutant Cade Carmichael both registered fifties, and while there were several promising partnerships, Bangladesh kept striking to keep the visitors in check.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford reports that it is another gorgeous day in Sylhet, though the humidity is up around 73 per cent and the wind has picked up compared to yesterday. Mentions that there was a little early movement for the seamers on Day 1, but it was all about the spinners. Shares that Hasan Murad got an average of 3.8 degrees of turn, the highest among the spinners, largely due to the slower pace he bowled at. Rainsford adds that Irish batters got in but couldn’t push on, and on this surface, conversion is key. States that the cracks have started to open up but nothing too concerning yet. Further says that there are runs to be had, but batters will need to grind them out.

Bangladesh's debutant, Hasan Murad is up next. Hasan says that he wanted to play for the team since 2023, but he never got a chance and he was always on the sidelines. Shares that he is happy to finally get a chance to play, and it's a great feeling.

Paul Stirling is in for a chat. He says the pitch started to turn a little more as the day went on. Feels they lost a couple more wickets than they would have liked, leaving the game evenly poised at this stage. He praises Cade Carmichael for playing brilliantly on debut, saying he’s someone who looks to have plenty of time at the crease. Stirling adds he’s slightly disappointed that neither Cade nor he could kick on to make a bigger contribution.

The final moments of Day 1 were a microcosm of the day's tension, with Bangladesh securing the eighth wicket on the very last ball. This late breakthrough gives the home side a psychological boost and a clear target as they will look to wrap up the tail quickly this morning. Barry McCarthy and the remaining batters will need to show great resolve to stretch the total. With the pitch expected to offer even more for the spinners as the game progresses, the pressure will soon shift onto Bangladesh's batters. Will Ireland add 30-40 more runs and get their total over 300, or will the Tigers roar to wrap up the innings in the first hour? We shall find out soon.

The visitors showed great character yesterday, especially through the impressive second-wicket partnership between Paul Stirling and the debutant Cade Carmichael, both of whom scored half-centuries to steady the innings after an early loss. However, Bangladesh's spin attack, led brilliantly by Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who claimed three wickets, kept them firmly in the game, striking at crucial moments to prevent a massive total.

Welcome back to Sylhet for Day 2 of what has already been an enthralling Test match so far! The first day gave us a fascinating contest that saw momentum swing back and forth. Ireland, after winning the toss and electing to bat, managed to post 270 runs on the board, but Bangladesh secured a vital upper hand by taking eight wickets.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

In the final session, Bangladesh did well and picked three wickets in the first half. However, just like we saw throughout the day, Ireland fought back and were on the verge of ending the day on a high but Jordan Neill fell on the final ball of the day and the hopes for a score around 300 lie solely on Barry McCarthy now. So, will the hosts take the remaining wickets in the first hour of Day 2? Or will the visitors take their total over 300? Join us tomorrow at 3.30 am GMT to find out, and a bit early for the build up of Day 2. Cheers!

Bangladesh fought back strongly in the second session, taking three wickets for 90 runs. Ireland, who started at 94/1, lost their key batters, Paul Stirling (60), and Cade Carmichael (59) was removed after a review, while Harry Tector fell for 1. Spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz was the best bowler of the second session with two wickets. Despite the setbacks, Curtis Campher and Lorcan Tucker survived the session to guide Ireland to the Tea break at 184/4.

That wicket on the final ball of the day proves how well Bangladesh have bowled today. Nonetheless, an evenly posied Day 1. Ireland dominated the opening session, reaching 94/1 at Lunch on Day 1 after winning the toss and electing to bat. Though Bangladesh struck early, dismissing captain Andy Balbirnie for a duck, they were let down by dropping three catches. Paul Stirling and debutant Cade Carmichael rebuilt the innings with a strong partnership, taking advantage of a good batting pitch and loose bowling to put Ireland in a strong position.

Bangladesh have been really poor on the field. They have dropped as many as four catches today. The bowlers have grinded hard but the fielding department has let them down. The session was a replica of the first one. Bangladesh scalped the wicket of Paul Stirling and Harry Tector in consecutive overs at the start of this session. Later, Najmul Hossain Shanto turned to the spin trio, Hasan Murad, Taijul Islam, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz for more wickets, but the pair of Lorcan Tucker and Curtis Campher showed a lot of character to end the session on a high. This could be an important phase of the Day. Can these two add more runs and end the day on a high? Stay tuned to find out how the last session unfolds.

Bangladesh started well with Hasan Mahmud dismissing Andy Balbirnie in the very first over but Paul Stirling and Cade Carmichael drew a lot of pressure before shifting gears swiftly and scoring runs. Bangladesh tried spinners from both ends but he didn't yield any dividends. Mehidy Hasan Miraz was introduced for the final over and we feel he can have a big say in this match. A good start by the visitors. Can they replicate the good work in the second session? Stay tuned to find out.

A cautious effort by Ireland and they have begun the first Test match really well. 94 runs scored in the session, with the majority coming from Paul Stirling's blade. Bangladesh’s fielding slump is a recurring issue.
